messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

message.content:
**Answer:**

The total entropy change for heating a 1 kg ice block from 0 °C to 100 °C at 1 atm (including melting, warming, and boiling) is

\[
\boxed{\Delta S \;\approx\; 8.6\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}}
\]

---

### How the number is obtained

| Stage | Process | ΔS (J K⁻¹) |
|-------|---------|------------|
| 1 | Ice → Water (melting) at 0 °C | \(m\,L_f/T_m = 1\,\text{kg}\times 334\,000\ \text{J kg}^{-1}/273.15\ \text{K} \approx 1.22\times10^{3}\) |
| 2 | Water (0 °C → 100 °C) | \(m\,c_p\,\ln(T_f/T_i) = 1\,\text{kg}\times 4180\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\times \ln(373.15/273.15) \approx 1.30\times10^{3}\) |
| 3 | Water → Steam (boiling) at 100 °C | \(m\,L_v/T_b = 1\,\text{kg}\times 2\,260\,000\ \text{J kg}^{-1}/373.15\ \text{K} \approx 6.06\times10^{3}\) |

Adding the three contributions:

\[
\Delta S_{\text{total}} = 1.22\times10^{3} + 1.30\times10^{3} + 6.06\times10^{3}
\approx 8.58\times10^{3}\ \text{J K}^{-1}
\]

Rounded to two significant figures, this is **8.6 kJ K⁻¹**.

---

### Quick reference values used

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Latent heat of fusion of water, \(L_f\) | 334 kJ kg⁻¹ |
| Latent heat of vaporization of water, \(L_v\) | 2260 kJ kg⁻¹ |
| Specific heat capacity of liquid water, \(c_p\) | 4.18 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| Melting temperature, \(T_m\) | 273.15 K |
| Boiling temperature, \(T_b\) | 373.15 K |

Feel free to ask if you’d like the calculation broken down further or if you want to see how the function could be used for each stage!
